Context: This excerpt from the charter issued by King James I describes the rights that the king granted to British colonists living in Virginia.
Title: Source 3: [Adapted from] the First Charter of Virginia (1606)
Content: The King of England grants and agrees that Sir Thomas Gates and others shall be called the First Colony. They may begin their `text(first)` plantation and residence at any place on the coast of Virginia or America where they think fit.
We also order that the colony shall have a council, which shall govern.
And there shall be a council established in England. It will have authority over all matters that concern the government.
Our subjects in the colonies and all of their children who are born there will have all liberties of a person living and born in England.
